---
title: "Authentication"
---

Here is the part that surprises people: you can send events to Umami all day without logging in. The ingestion endpoint is public, because a browser tracker on a public web page cannot keep a secret. Credentials only enter the picture when you want to read data back out.

When you do, there are two doors and you walk through exactly one of them. A self-hosted instance takes a username and password and hands you a token. Umami Cloud takes an API key. The package routes requests and sets headers differently behind each door, so the choice matters even though the rest of your code stays identical.

## What needs a credential

| Call | Needs | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `new_event()`, `new_page_view()`, `new_revenue_event()` | `set_url_base()` or a Cloud key | Umami's `/api/send` endpoint is unauthenticated. |
| `heartbeat()` | `set_url_base()` or a Cloud key | Self-hosted pings `/api/heartbeat`. Cloud calls `/me` with the key. |
| `websites()`, `website_stats()`, `active_users()` | `login()` or a Cloud key | These read data and require a token or key. |
| `verify_token()` | `login()` or a Cloud key | Returns `False` rather than raising when nothing is set. |

Call a query function before you have a credential and you get `umami.errors.OperationNotAllowedError` with the message `Call login() or set_cloud_api_key() before proceeding.` No request is made; the package checks before it dials.

## Self-hosted: set_url_base and login

```python
import umami

umami.set_url_base('https://umami.example.com')
login = umami.login('admin', 'super-secret')
print(login.user.username, login.user.isAdmin)
```

`login()` posts to `/api/auth/login`, stores the returned token in the module, and returns a `LoginResponse` with the token and a `User` model. You can drop the return value on the floor. Every later query call sends the stored token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` without you touching it.

Both arguments must be non-empty, and whitespace does not count, or `ValidationError` is raised before any request. Wrong credentials come back from the server as a 401 and raise `httpx2.HTTPStatusError`.

Calling `login()` again replaces the stored token. There is no logout function; the token lives until the process exits or you log in again.

### Tokens expire

Umami login tokens are temporary, and they expire on Umami's schedule, not yours. A long-running process should assume that one day a query call will start failing with a 401, probably during a demo. `verify_token()` asks the server whether the stored token is still good and never raises:

```python
if not umami.verify_token():
    umami.login('admin', 'super-secret')
```

`verify_token(check_server=False)` skips the network and only reports whether a credential is present, which is the same answer `is_logged_in()` gives.

## Umami Cloud: set_cloud_api_key

```python
import umami

umami.set_cloud_api_key('your-cloud-api-key', region='eu')  # region is optional
umami.set_website_id('978435e2-7ba1-4337-9860-ec31ece2db60')
umami.set_hostname('example.com')
```

Create the key in the Umami Cloud dashboard under the API keys settings. `region` accepts `'us'`, `'eu'`, or `None`; when omitted, Cloud uses the region of the account that owns the key. Any other value raises `ValidationError`, as does a blank key.

Setting a key flips three switches at once:

- Query and verification calls go to `https://api.umami.is/v1`, with `/eu` or `/us` inserted after `v1` when you pin a region, and carry an `x-umami-api-key` header.
- Events go to `https://cloud.umami.is/api/send` with no credential, because the Cloud ingestion endpoint is public too. The region does not affect this host.
- `login()` and `login_async()` raise `OperationNotAllowedError`. The key is the credential, and Cloud has no username and password login to call.

You do not call `set_url_base()` in Cloud mode. If you do, the value is stored and politely ignored while the key is set.

## Switching modes

`clear_cloud_api_key()` removes the key and the region, and everything reverts to self-hosted behaviour: events use `url_base`, and query calls need a login token. A token from a `login()` made before you switched to Cloud is still sitting there, so you do not have to log in again.

`is_logged_in()` returns `True` when either a login token or a Cloud key is set. It does not contact the server; use `verify_token()` for that.

## Keep credentials out of code

Read the password or key from an environment variable or a secrets store at startup, then hand it to `login()` or `set_cloud_api_key()`. The package does not read any environment variables itself, so there is no magic name to discover and no surprise when a variable is set on the wrong machine.

```python
import os
import umami

umami.set_url_base(os.environ['UMAMI_URL'])
umami.login(os.environ['UMAMI_USER'], os.environ['UMAMI_PASSWORD'])
```

If a login fails, [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd#login-and-token-problems) lists the causes.
